bug_description.normalized: The staged 83-byte BER/DER PKCS#12 witness imports successfully and later reaches gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse bag index 0. gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag decodes the outer AuthenticatedSafe, sees that the first entry contentType is pkcs7-data, and passes that entry's inner SafeContents OCTET STRING into _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents. Inside that function, stack buffer oid is allocated without initialization and reused first for SafeBag bagId parsing and then for bag-attribute dispatch. The first SafeBag bagId bytes in the staged PoC are exactly 06 01 F7; asn1_read_value succeeds, oid2bag(oid) maps that unrecognized OID to GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN (20), and the bag_type < 0 abort is skipped, so bag-attribute parsing continues. The first bag-attribute type bytes are exactly 06 02 2A F2; _gnutls_x509_decode_and_read_attribute reads that attribute's .type into the same oid buffer, and the saved MSAN trace shows bytes from offset 4 remain uninitialized when strcmp(oid, KEY_ID_OID) performs its 22-byte compare. The staged artifacts do not establish the real fix: sample metadata lists commit 470a4e82449bb3920adb554151cf763722ff472e and patch.diff records d165c2a37f7d072cc88db88ec97f057a9ac6e4aa, but neither touches lib/x509/pkcs12.c or the PKCS#12 path.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled DER witness and materializes it into the PKCS#12 ASN.1 tree later traversed by gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag.
source.value_from: The staged poc is an 83-byte BER/DER PKCS#12 blob whose imported ASN.1 tree contains an outer DATA_OID authSafe, an inner AuthenticatedSafe entry with contentType pkcs7-data, a first SafeBag bagId encoded as 06 01 F7, and a first bag-attribute type encoded as 06 02 2A F2. Those bytes are preserved in pkcs12->pkcs12 and later re-read during bag extraction.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: oid is a stack buffer allocated without initialization. The later bag-attribute read reuses this buffer without clearing it, and the saved MSAN trace shows bytes from offset 4 are still uninitialized when strcmp reads oid.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. After a successful bag-attribute decode, the dispatch compares the partially initialized stack buffer oid against the 21-character KEY_ID_OID literal, and the compare consumes oid's uninitialized tail.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 4 inside a 22-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of oid in _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents.

root_cause.description: The SafeBag dispatch buffer oid is stack-allocated without zero-initialization and then reused across bagId parsing and bag-attribute parsing; on the staged witness, the later attribute read does not make the whole buffer defined, so strcmp(oid, KEY_ID_OID) reads bytes MSAN still marks uninitialized.
root_cause.note: _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents assumes oid is safe for fixed-literal strcmp dispatch, but it never clears the buffer before bagId parsing or the later attribute read. On the staged witness, bagId bytes 06 01 F7 survive the bag_type gate via GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN, and attribute bytes 06 02 2A F2 are then read into the same oid buffer before the KEY_ID_OID comparison. The saved MSAN trace ties the sink back to the oid stack allocation and reports the first uninitialized byte at offset 4 in the compare window. A correct fix zero-initializes oid before these reads or avoids fixed-literal strcmp on partially initialized storage.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness's first AuthenticatedSafe entry has contentType pkcs7-data, so gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag takes the _parse_safe_contents() path and enters the vulnerable SafeContents decoder instead of the encrypted-bag path.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled PKCS#12 bytes and materializes them as the ASN.1 tree pkcs12->pkcs12. The staged witness preserves the outer DATA_OID authSafe, the first inner pkcs7-data entry, the first SafeBag bagId bytes 06 01 F7, and the first bag-attribute type bytes 06 02 2A F2 for later PKCS#12 decoding.
simple_parse starts its search with idx == 0 and asks for the first bag from the imported PKCS#12 object, making the witness-controlled first AuthenticatedSafe entry reachable.
Decodes the imported outer authSafe into ASN.1 tree c2 representing the inner AuthenticatedSafe sequence from which bag 0 is selected.

After setting root2 to ?1.contentType, get_bag reads the first AuthenticatedSafe member's contentType into oid. Static ASN.1 parsing of the staged PoC shows this OID is pkcs7-data, so the data bag path is selected.

fine_trace.code: snprintf(root2, sizeof(root2), "?%u.content", indx + 1); if (strcmp(oid, DATA_OID) == 0) { result = _parse_safe_contents(c2, root2, bag); goto cleanup; }
fine_trace.note: The first entry's contentType matches DATA_OID, so get_bag targets ?1.content and calls _parse_safe_contents on the unencrypted SafeContents payload instead of treating the bag as encrypted.

Extracts the selected ?1.content OCTET STRING into content. These attacker-controlled SafeContents bytes contain the first SafeBag bagId bytes 06 01 F7 and the first bag-attribute type bytes 06 02 2A F2 that later drive the vulnerable dispatch.

Allocates the stack buffer later used for bag-attribute dispatch without initializing it. MemorySanitizer identifies this stack allocation in _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents as the origin of the poisoned bytes consumed at the sink.
Decodes the attacker-controlled SafeContents bytes into ASN.1 tree c2, exposing the first SafeBag's ?1.bagId and ?1.bagAttributes.?1.type entries for the later gates and attribute dispatch.

After setting root to ?1.bagId, the function reads the first SafeBag's bagId into oid. The staged witness encodes those bytes as 06 01 F7; the later oid2bag result shows this read succeeded and yielded an unrecognized bag OID string that is carried forward in oid.

Maps the bagId OID to a bag type and checks the abort gate. oid2bag returns GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN (20) for any unrecognized OID, so this staged bagId survives as bag_type >= 0 and parsing continues into bagValue and bagAttributes instead of aborting.

In the first bagAttributes iteration, the helper reads ?1.bagAttributes.?1.type into the same oid buffer without clearing it first. The staged PoC encodes that attribute type as 06 02 2A F2; combined with the saved MSAN report that bytes from offset 4 are still uninitialized at the following strcmp, this successful helper call leaves oid not fully defined before dispatch.

MSAN sink. KEY_ID_OID is the 21-character literal 1.2.840.113549.1.9.21, so strcmp invokes __interceptor_memcmp on a 22-byte region. Because the first poisoned byte is still at oid[4], the compare reads the uninitialized tail and reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of oid in the stack frame of _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents; the actual oid declaration is line 372.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: Sample metadata lists fix commit 470a4e82449bb3920adb554151cf763722ff472e and the staged patch.diff records d165c2a37f7d072cc88db88ec97f057a9ac6e4aa, but neither artifact touches lib/x509/pkcs12.c, _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents, _parse_safe_contents, gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag, or the PKCS#12 fuzzer. The actual remediation is therefore unavailable in the staged evidence, and the provided patch bundle cannot be used as fix proof for this MSAN crash.

poc.trigger: The staged witness imports as PKCS#12, reaches gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse bag 0, decodes the first AuthenticatedSafe entry as pkcs7-data, survives the first SafeBag bagId gate with bytes 06 01 F7, and then decodes a first bag-attribute type whose bytes are exactly 06 02 2A F2. _pkcs12_decode_safe_contents reads that short attribute OID into stack buffer oid and immediately compares oid to KEY_ID_OID, triggering MSAN on oid's uninitialized tail.

format.name: DER/BER PKCS#12 with malformed SafeBag attribute OID
format.contract: A PKCS#12 blob that imports successfully, reaches gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse bag index 0, uses an outer and first-inner contentType of pkcs7-data, encodes the first SafeBag bagId exactly as DER bytes 06 01 F7 so oid2bag returns GNUTLS_BAG_UNKNOWN, and encodes the first bag-attribute type exactly as DER bytes 06 02 2A F2. On the staged vulnerable path, that exact nested shape causes _gnutls_x509_decode_and_read_attribute to leave bytes in oid still uninitialized before strcmp(oid, KEY_ID_OID) performs the 22-byte compare reported by MSAN. The verified trigger is this exact malformed witness shape observed in the staged poc, not a generalized class of all invalid PKCS#12 files.
